nodes.label: Asia
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Largest continent covering one-third of total land area. Lies in Eastern Hemisphere. Tropic of Cancer passes through it. Separated from Europe by Ural Mountains. Together called Eurasia.

nodes.label: Hydrosphere
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Domain of water comprising all forms: ice, liquid water and water vapour. Covers more than 71% of earth's surface. Over 97% is salty ocean water; only about 2.7% is fresh water.

nodes.label: Africa
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Second largest continent. Only continent through which Tropic of Cancer, Equator and Tropic of Capricorn all pass. Contains Sahara, the world's largest hot desert, and Nile, the longest river.

nodes.label: Southern Ocean
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Encircles Antarctica and extends northward to 60 degrees south latitude. Also called the Antarctic Ocean.

nodes.label: Arctic Ocean
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Located within Arctic Circle, surrounds North Pole. Connected with Pacific Ocean by Bering Strait. Bound by northern coasts of North America and Eurasia.

nodes.label: Australia
nodes.subject: geography
nodes.detail: Smallest continent, entirely in Southern Hemisphere. Surrounded on all sides by oceans and seas. Called an island continent.
